tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on The Muscular System

questions.question: Name the antagonistic pair at the elbow joint and identify the agonist during flexion.
questions.correctAnswer: The antagonistic pair at the elbow is the biceps and triceps. The agonist during flexion is the biceps (it contracts to flex the elbow while the triceps relaxes).

questions.question: Explain the difference between concentric and eccentric isotonic contraction, giving a sporting example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Concentric: the muscle shortens while contracting - e.g. the quadriceps shortening during the upward phase of a squat. Eccentric: the muscle lengthens while contracting - e.g. the quadriceps lengthening during the controlled downward phase of a squat.

questions.question: What is the role of a fixator muscle? Give an example from a sporting action.
questions.correctAnswer: A fixator stabilises the origin of the agonist muscle so it can work effectively. During a bicep curl, the deltoids contract isometrically to hold the shoulder still while the biceps works on the elbow.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on The Muscular System

questions.question: During the downward phase of a squat, which type of contraction are the quadriceps performing? Explain why.
questions.correctAnswer: Eccentric contraction. The quadriceps are lengthening (the knee is flexing as the body lowers) but the muscle is still under tension to control the speed of descent.

questions.question: Which muscle is the agonist at the elbow during the pushing phase of a press-up?
questions.correctAnswer: The triceps is the agonist at the elbow during the pushing phase (it contracts concentrically to extend the elbow).

questions.question: Explain why Type I muscle fibres are more suited to marathon running than Type IIx fibres.
questions.correctAnswer: Type I fibres are slow-contracting with high fatigue resistance, high myoglobin and mitochondria density, making them ideal for endurance events. Marathon running requires sustained aerobic effort over 26.2 miles. Type IIx fibres fatigue quickly and rely on anaerobic energy, making them unsuitable for prolonged exercise.
